mainTopic: What a woman may wear or carry on her body outside on שבת: cloths, mouth items, false teeth, a healing coin, girls' ear threads and fastened cloaks, plus the strict practices of שמואל's father.
overview: This amud opens with the end of a ברייתא about spreading wet clothes in the sun. It shows that תנאים argue whether a מראית העין ban applies even in private. The גמרא then explains our משנה's list of things a woman may wear outside on שבת. A מוך in the ear or sandal must be tied, but a menstrual מוך need not be, because it is repulsive and she will not carry it. Two great sages went out with untied ear cloths, and the גמרא explains that a cloth pressed in tightly needs no tying. The גמרא explains the pepper, salt and spices in her mouth, and limits the dispute about a false tooth to gold only. אביי shows that רבי, רבי אליעזר and רבי שמעון בן אלעזר share one idea: a woman will not take off and show an item whose removal makes her look bad. A new משנה permits a coin on a foot wound, threads in girls' ears, veils and fastened cloaks. The גמרא explains why a סלע heals the wound. It then tells of שמואל's father's strict practices with his daughters, and that discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The tail of the ברייתא: spread clothes in the sun, but not in front of people
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends: one may spread wet clothes in the sun, but not where people can see. רבי אליעזר and רבי שמעון forbid it entirely.
steps.simpleTranslation: He may spread them out in the sun, but not in front of people. רבי אליעזר and רבי שמעון forbid it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a ברייתא it began quoting on the previous amud. The ברייתא shows that תנאים argue about whether something forbidden because of מראית העין is also forbidden in private.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the first opinion, the only problem is that people might see the clothes and think he washed them, so in a hidden place it is allowed. רבי אליעזר and רבי שמעון forbid it even in private. This means they hold that a גזירה of מראית העין applies everywhere, even בחדרי חדרים. The ברייתא shows that this question is a real מחלוקת among תנאים.

keyTerms.meaning: In front of the people, where others can see
A ban based on how an action looks to onlookers

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not the start of a new topic. It is the end of a ברייתא that began on the previous amud, so it belongs to the previous discussion about מראית העין and not to the משנה about the מוך.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא is a classic source for the question of whether a מראית העין prohibition applies even in total privacy.

phrases.english: He may spread them out in the sun,
but not in front of the people.
phrases.notes: People might suspect he washed them on the holy day.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Shimon forbid it.

steps.triggerLanguage: שׁוֹטְחָן בַּחַמָּה, אֲבָל לֹא כְּנֶגֶד הָעָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a ברייתא begun earlier as a source for a מחלוקת תנאים.
steps.raayaObject: That whether מראית העין applies even in private is a מחלוקת among תנאים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא: the first opinion allows spreading clothes in private, while רבי אליעזר and רבי שמעון forbid it.

steps.title: A cloth in her ear must be tied
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's allowance of a מוך in a woman's ear. רמי בר יחזקאל adds that this applies only when the cloth is tied to her ear.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said a woman may go out 'with a מוך that is in her ear.' רמי בר יחזקאל taught: that is only when it is tied to her ear.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to our משנה and quotes its first case. A ברייתא from רמי בר יחזקאל then narrows the case so that it applies only when the cloth is tied on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An untied cloth could fall out. She might then pick it up and carry it in the public domain on שבת. Tying it keeps it attached to her, so there is no risk of carrying.

keyTerms.meaning: A soft wad of cloth or cotton
And that is only when; introduces a limiting condition

phrases.english: And with a cloth that is in her ear.
Rami bar Yechezkel taught:
And that is only where it is tied to her ear.
phrases.notes: So it will not fall and be carried.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבְמוֹךְ שֶׁבְּאׇזְנָהּ. תָּנֵי רָמֵי בַּר יְחֶזְקֵאל: וְהוּא שֶׁקָּשׁוּר בְּאׇזְנָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from the ברייתא back to explaining our משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מוך in the ear is allowed on שבת only if it is tied.

steps.title: A cloth in her sandal must be tied
steps.stepSummary: The same pattern applies to the second case in the משנה: a מוך in her sandal is allowed only when tied to the sandal.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said 'with a מוך that is in her sandal.' רמי בר יחזקאל taught: that is only when it is tied to her sandal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's second case. רמי בר יחזקאל applies the same 'must be tied' condition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reasoning is the same as for the ear. If the cloth slips out of the sandal, she might pick it up and carry it. Tying it to the sandal removes that worry.

keyTerms.meaning: Lest she carry it (the underlying worry)

phrases.english: And with a cloth that is in her sandal.
Rami bar Yechezkel taught:
And that is only where it is tied to her sandal.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבְמוֹךְ שֶׁבְּסַנְדָּלָהּ. תָּנֵי רָמֵי בַּר יְחֶזְקֵאל: וְהוּא שֶׁקָּשׁוּר לָהּ בְּסַנְדָּלָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel clarification for the next case in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מוך in the sandal is allowed on שבת only if it is tied.

steps.title: The third case: a cloth prepared for her menstrual flow
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's third case, a מוך the woman prepared for her נדה flow, to set up a discussion of whether it too must be tied.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said 'with a מוך that she prepared for her menstrual flow.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא quotes the third case of the משנה so it can ask whether the same 'tied' requirement applies here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After two cases that required tying, we naturally expect the same rule here. The next two steps test that expectation.

keyTerms.meaning: A burden; something carried rather than worn

phrases.english: And with a cloth that she prepared for herself for her menstrual flow.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next case of the משנה, preparing the next discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה allows a woman to go out with a מוך placed for her נדה flow.

steps.title: רמי בר חמא assumes it must be tied between her thighs
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא considered saying that, like the other cases, the menstrual cloth is allowed only when tied between her thighs.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא thought to say: that is only when it is tied between her thighs.
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר חמא offers a first assumption that copies the 'must be tied' rule from the earlier cases. The phrase סבר למימר signals that this view will be corrected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His logic is consistent: if a loose cloth in the ear or sandal is a problem, a loose menstrual cloth should be one too. This is the הוה אמינא that רבא is about to reject.

keyTerms.meaning: He thought to say; marks an initial assumption that will be rejected

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up רמי בר יחזקאל (who required tying for the ear and sandal) with רמי בר חמא (whose view about the menstrual cloth is rejected).

phrases.english: Rami bar Chama thought to say,
and that is only where it is tied to her between her thighs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the earlier 'tied' rule to the third case as an initial assumption.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Initial assumption: the menstrual cloth is allowed only when tied.

steps.title: רבא: no tying needed, because she won't carry a repulsive cloth
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that the menstrual cloth is allowed even if untied. Since it is repulsive, she will not pick it up and carry it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: even though it is not tied to her, since it is repulsive, she will not come to carry it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא rejects רמי בר חמא's assumption and explains why this case is different from the ear and sandal cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason for tying was the worry that a fallen cloth would be picked up and carried. A soiled menstrual cloth is disgusting, so no one would pick it up and carry it. Without that worry, there is no need for tying.

keyTerms.meaning: She will not come to carry it

steps.whatToRemember: A מוך in the ear or sandal must be tied, so it won't fall and be carried. The menstrual מוך need not be tied, because it is מאיס and she won't carry it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that a גזירה applies only where its reason applies. When the fear of carrying is gone, the extra condition falls away.

phrases.english: Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינוֹ קָשׁוּר לָהּ,
phrases.english: even though it is not tied to her,
since it is repulsive,
she will not come to carry it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינוֹ קָשׁוּר לָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רמי בר חמא's assumption.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the requirement that the menstrual מוך be tied.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The reason for tying (fear of carrying) does not apply to a repulsive object.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The menstrual מוך is allowed even when untied.

steps.title: What if she made a handle for the menstrual cloth?
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה asks רבי אבא whether the menstrual cloth is still allowed if she made a handle for it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה asked רבי אבא: If she made herself a handgrip for the cloth, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a follow-up question about רבא's rule from the previous step. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא allowed the untied menstrual cloth because it is repulsive, so she will not pick it up. A handle lets her hold it without touching the dirty cloth. The question is whether this removes the 'repulsive' protection, so that we should now worry she will carry it.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked of him (introduces a question to a teacher)

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה מֵרַבִּי אַבָּא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya asked of Rabbi Abba:
If she made herself a handgrip, what is the law?
phrases.notes: Refers to the menstrual cloth from the previous step

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה מֵרַבִּי אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the limit of רבא's reasoning (the cloth is repulsive) from step 6
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a handle, which removes the need to touch the repulsive cloth, cancel the permission to go out with it untied?

steps.title: It is still permitted
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא answers that even with a handle, it is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא answers the question: the cloth is allowed even if she made a handle for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The handle does not change the result. The cloth itself is still repulsive, so we still do not worry that she will take it off and carry it.

phrases.english: He said to him: It is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Even with a handle, going out with the menstrual cloth is permitted

steps.title: רבי יוחנן said the same thing
steps.stepSummary: A report in the name of רבי יוחנן supports רבי אבא's answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also stated: רב נחמן בר אושעיא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: If she made herself a handgrip, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support for רבי אבא's answer. The same ruling was also reported in the name of רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No new law is added here. The ruling of step 8 is confirmed by an independent source, so we see it is not one teacher's private opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also stated (a supporting report from another אמורא)

phrases.english: It was also stated:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר אוֹשַׁעְיָא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Oshaya said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
If she made herself a handgrip, it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of step 8
steps.raayaObject: The ruling that a handle does not make the cloth forbidden
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן, as reported by רב נחמן בר אושעיא
steps.whatToRemember: The menstrual cloth is allowed even untied, and even with a handle, because it is repulsive and she will not carry it.

steps.title: Great sages went out with untied ear cloths
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן went to the בית מדרש, and רבי ינאי went into a כרמלית, with cloths in their ears. Their colleagues disagreed with them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן went out with them (cloths in his ears) to the study hall, and his colleagues disagree with him. רבי ינאי went out with them to a כרמלית, and his whole generation disagrees with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the ear cloth from the משנה and reports what two great sages actually did. This report sets up a question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The colleagues disagreed because the cloths were not tied, so they held it was forbidden. A כרמלית is an in-between area, neither fully public nor private, where carrying is forbidden מדרבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: Went out with them (the ear cloths)
An in-between domain where carrying is rabbinically forbidden

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think 'בהו' (with them) means the menstrual cloth. The גמרא has switched back to the cloth in the ear.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן נָפֵיק בְּהוּ לְבֵי מִדְרְשָׁא,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan went out with them to the study hall,
and his colleagues disagree with him.
Rabbi Yannai went out with them to a karmelit,
and all of his generation disagree with him.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן נָפֵיק בְּהוּ לְבֵי מִדְרְשָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the ear cloth discussed in step 2
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן and רבי ינאי went out with untied ear cloths, against the view of their colleagues

steps.title: But רמי בר יחזקאל requires the cloth to be tied
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how these sages could go out with untied cloths when רמי בר יחזקאל taught that it must be tied.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רמי בר יחזקאל teach: And that is only when it is tied to her ear!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the sages' behavior. It points out that this contradicts רמי בר יחזקאל's rule from step 2.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רמי בר יחזקאל allowed the ear cloth only if it is tied, so that it cannot fall out and be carried. רבי יוחנן and רבי ינאי went out with untied cloths, which seems to break this rule.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't he teach? (opens a challenge from a teaching)

phrases.english: But didn't Rami bar Yeḥezkel teach:
And that is when it is tied to her ear!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the sages' conduct reported in step 10
steps.kashyaTarget: The conduct of רבי יוחנן and רבי ינאי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An untied cloth was required to be tied according to רמי בר יחזקאל, so going out with it should be forbidden

steps.title: Stuck in tightly versus not tightly
steps.stepSummary: The sages' cloths were pressed tightly into the ear. רמי בר יחזקאל was speaking of a loose cloth.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult: this case is where it is stuck in tightly, and that case is where it is not stuck in tightly.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by splitting the cases. The two sources are talking about different situations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the cloth is pressed tightly into the ear, it will not fall out, so tying is not needed. רמי בר יחזקאל's rule that it must be tied applies only to a loose cloth that could fall out.

keyTerms.meaning: This case ... that case (splitting into two situations)

steps.whatToRemember: An ear cloth is allowed if it is tied or if it is pressed in tightly. A loose, untied ear cloth is forbidden.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this is where it is stuck in tightly,
that is where it is not stuck in tightly.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא דְּמִיהַדַּק, הָא דְּלָא מִיהַדַּק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 11
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any untied ear cloth is forbidden, so the sages acted against the rule
steps.terutzMaskana: A tightly pressed cloth needs no tying. Only a loose one must be tied.

steps.title: Why pepper and salt are in her mouth
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about pepper and a grain of salt and explains what each is for.
steps.simpleTranslation: With pepper and with a grain of salt: pepper is for mouth odor, and a grain of salt is for a toothache.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next case in the משנה and explains why a woman would keep these items in her mouth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both items serve a real purpose, one for breath and one for pain. So they count as things she uses on her body, not as items she is carrying.

phrases.english: With pepper and with a grain of salt.
Pepper is for mouth odor,
a grain of salt is for a toothache.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next case in the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Pepper is for bad breath, and salt is for a toothache

steps.title: What 'anything in her mouth' means
steps.stepSummary: The משנה's phrase 'anything she puts in her mouth' refers to ginger or cinnamon.
steps.simpleTranslation: And anything that she puts into her mouth: this means ginger, or alternatively cinnamon.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's general phrase and gives examples of what it includes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The general phrase is explained with real examples. These are spices kept in the mouth for a purpose, like the pepper in the step before.

phrases.english: And anything that she puts into her mouth.
Ginger, or alternatively, cinnamon.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues explaining the mouth items in the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'Anything in her mouth' means ginger or cinnamon

steps.title: The משנה's dispute about a false or gold tooth
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: רבי permits going out with a false tooth or a gold tooth, and the חכמים forbid it.
steps.simpleTranslation: A false tooth, a gold tooth: רבי permits, and the חכמים forbid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next case in the משנה. This sets up רבי זירא's comment in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry is that she might take the tooth out to show it off and then carry it. רבי is not worried about this, but the חכמים are.

keyTerms.meaning: רבי permits and the חכמים forbid

phrases.english: A false tooth, a gold tooth,
Rabbi permits and the Rabbis prohibit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next case in the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי and the חכמים disagree about going out with a false or gold tooth

steps.title: The dispute is only about gold, not silver
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא says the argument is only about a gold tooth. Everyone permits a silver tooth.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: They taught this dispute only about a gold tooth, but about a silver one, everyone agrees it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא narrows the dispute of the משנה to gold teeth only.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Gold is precious, so the חכמים worry she will take it out to show her friends and end up carrying it. Silver is not as impressive, so no one worries about that, and everyone permits it.

keyTerms.meaning: They taught this only regarding (limits a teaching)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume that a false tooth of any metal is in dispute. According to רבי זירא, silver is allowed by everyone.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:
They only taught this regarding gold,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל בְּשֶׁל כֶּסֶף דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל מוּתָּר.
phrases.english: but regarding silver, everyone agrees it is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁל זָהָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the dispute quoted in step 15
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only a gold tooth is in dispute. A silver tooth is permitted by all.

steps.title: A ברייתא confirms רבי זירא
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא states the same thing: silver is permitted by everyone, and only gold is in dispute.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way: with silver, everyone agrees it is permitted. With gold, רבי permits and the חכמים forbid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports רבי זירא's limit on the dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא spells out openly what רבי זירא said: silver is permitted by all, and the argument is only about gold. So his reading of the משנה is confirmed by a תנאי source.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way (a ברייתא supports the statement)

steps.whatToRemember: A silver tooth is permitted by everyone. A gold tooth is a dispute between רבי (permits) and the חכמים (forbid), because she might take it out to show it off.

phrases.english: It was also taught this way:
With silver, everyone agrees it is permitted.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁל זָהָב, רַבִּי מַתִּיר וַחֲכָמִים אוֹסְרִין.
phrases.english: With gold, Rabbi permits and the Rabbis prohibit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי זירא's statement in step 16
steps.raayaObject: רבי זירא's claim that only a gold tooth is in dispute

steps.title: אביי: three תנאים share one principle
steps.stepSummary: אביי says רבי, רבי אליעזר and רבי שמעון בן אלעזר all hold that a woman won't remove something whose removal makes her unappealing.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: רבי, רבי אליעזר and רבי שמעון בן אלעזר all hold that anything whose removal would make her look bad, she will not come to take off and show.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי takes רבי's view about the gold tooth and says two other תנאים think the same way. This sets up the next steps, where the גמרא shows where each one says it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The usual worry with jewelry on שבת is that she will take it off to show a friend and then carry it in public. אביי says that worry does not apply when removing the item would expose a flaw, like a missing tooth. She would rather keep it on.

keyTerms.meaning: They hold / they are of the opinion
She becomes unappealing because of it (when it is removed)

steps.whyThisMatters: This one principle explains three separate rulings by different תנאים. It gives us a general rule for which items are allowed to be worn outside.

phrases.english: Abaye said:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר
phrases.english: Rabbi, and Rabbi Eliezer, and Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar
all of them hold
that anything by which she becomes unappealing (if removed)
phrases.notes: For example, taking out a false tooth reveals a gap.

phrases.english: she will not come to (take it off and) show it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: רַבִּי וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר כּוּלְּהוּ סְבִירָא לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Generalizes רבי's lenient view on the gold tooth into a principle shared with other תנאים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An item whose removal makes her unappealing will not be removed to show off, so going out with it is permitted.

steps.title: Sources for רבי and רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: רבי's view is the gold tooth case just discussed. רבי אליעזר's view is a ברייתא exempting a woman who goes out with a fragrance bundle or a balsam flask.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי: that which we said. רבי אליעזר: as it was taught: רבי אליעזר exempts a woman who goes out with a bundle of fragrant herbs and with a flask of balsam oil.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up אביי's claim. It points to where רבי and רבי אליעזר show this principle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי, the source is the false or gold tooth he permitted. For רבי אליעזר, a woman who wears perfume because she has a bad odor will not take it off to show it, because her smell would then be noticed. That is why he exempts her.

keyTerms.meaning: A small flask of balsam oil (perfume)

phrases.english: Rabbi: that which we said (the gold tooth).
Rabbi Eliezer: as it was taught (in a ברייתא):
Rabbi Eliezer exempts (a woman who goes out) with a bundle of fragrant herbs
and with a flask of balsam oil.
phrases.notes: A woman who needs perfume to cover a bad odor won't remove it in public.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי — הָא דַּאֲמַרַן. רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר — דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the sources for the first two names in אביי's list.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's claim that רבי and רבי אליעזר hold the principle
steps.raayaSupportSource: The earlier משנה (gold tooth) and a ברייתא about perfume bundles

steps.title: Source for רבי שמעון בן אלעזר: under the hairnet
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר rules that anything worn under the hairnet is permitted, and anything worn over it is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר: as it was taught: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר stated a rule: anything that is beneath the net, she may go out with it. Above the net, she may not go out with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the third source, completing אביי's proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An ornament under her hairnet cannot be shown without uncovering her hair in public, which she would never do. So there is no worry she will remove it. An item worn over the net is easy to take off and show, so it is forbidden.
steps.whatToRemember: All three תנאים agree on one rule: if taking the item off would embarrass or expose her, there is no fear she will remove and carry it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar: as it was taught,

phrases.aramaic: כְּלָל אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar stated a rule:
anything that is beneath the hairnet,
she may go out with it,
above the hairnet,
she may not go out with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר — דְּתַנְיָא, כְּלָל אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the list of sources for אביי's principle.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's claim that רבי שמעון בן אלעזר holds the principle
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא with רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's rule about the hairnet

steps.title: New משנה: coin on a wound, and girls' ear threads
steps.stepSummary: A woman may go out with a coin tied on a foot wound. Young girls may go out with threads or wood chips in their ears.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: She may go out with a סלע coin that is on a wound. Young girls may go out with threads, and even with wood chips that are in their ears.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists more items that are allowed to be worn outside on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The coin is treated as a healing bandage, not as something being carried. The threads and chips keep newly pierced ear holes from closing, so they serve the body and are not a load.

keyTerms.meaning: Abbreviation for מתניתין: here begins the משנה
A wound or sore (on the foot)

phrases.english: Mishnah:
She may go out with a sela coin that is (tied) on a wound.
Young girls may go out with threads,
and even with wood chips that are in their ears.
phrases.notes: These keep the pierced holes from closing until earrings are put in.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה that continues the list of permitted items.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A coin on a wound, and threads or chips in girls' ears, are permitted outside on שבת.

steps.title: Veils and fastened cloaks are permitted for everyone
steps.stepSummary: Arabian women may go out veiled and Median women with fastened cloaks. The same applies to anyone; the חכמים just described the common practice.
steps.simpleTranslation: Arabian women may go out veiled, and Median women with fastened cloaks, and so may any person. The חכמים simply spoke about what is common.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה permits regional styles of dress. It then clarifies that the permission is not limited to those places.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Naming Arabia and Media might suggest the rule applies only there. The משנה adds that the חכמים spoke about the usual case, and the law is the same for anyone dressed this way.

keyTerms.meaning: With cloaks fastened (around a stone or similar)
The Sages spoke about the common, current situation

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think this rule is only for Arabian or Median women. The משנה explicitly says it applies to any person.

phrases.english: Arabian women may go out veiled
and Median women with fastened cloaks,
and (so may) any person;
it is just that the Sages spoke of the common case.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list of permitted items.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Veils and fastened cloaks are permitted for everyone, not only in the places named.

steps.title: Fastening a cloak around a stone, nut or coin
steps.stepSummary: She may fasten her cloak around a stone, nut or coin, but she should not do the fastening on שבת itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: She may fasten (her cloak) on a stone, on a nut, or on a coin, as long as she does not fasten it from the start on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה explains how the cloak may be fastened and adds one limit on doing it on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wrapping the cloak around a small object makes it work like a button, so the object counts as part of the garment. However, she should not set up this fastening for the first time on שבת itself.

keyTerms.meaning: She fastens (the cloak, like a button)

steps.whatToRemember: A small object wrapped into a cloak as a button becomes part of the garment, but the fastening should not be done on שבת itself.

phrases.english: She may fasten (her cloak) on a stone
and on a nut and on a coin,
as long as she does not fasten (it)
from the outset on Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: פּוֹרֶפֶת עַל הָאֶבֶן וְעַל הָאֱגוֹז וְעַל הַמַּטְבֵּעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the 'fastened cloaks' are fastened and adds a limitation.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Fastening a cloak around a stone, nut or coin is permitted, but she should not fasten it initially on שבת.

steps.title: What is a צינית?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins by asking what the word צינית in the משנה means.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is a צינית?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its discussion by asking what a word in the משנה means. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה allowed a woman to go out with a coin on a צינית, but it never explained the word. Before we can understand the rule, we need to know what condition she is treating.

keyTerms.meaning: A word from the משנה that the גמרא is defining

phrases.english: GEMARA:
What is a tzinit?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the coin-on-a-wound case from the משנה (step 21) to define its term.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the word צינית.

steps.title: A צינית is a sore on the sole of the foot
steps.stepSummary: צינית means בת ארעא, a wound on the bottom of the foot.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a 'daughter of the ground,' meaning a sore on the sole of the foot.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question. A צינית is a sore on the bottom of the foot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase בת ארעא literally means 'daughter of the ground.' It gets this name because the sore is on the part of the foot that touches the ground. Now we know the coin is a medical treatment worn on the foot.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'daughter of the ground'; a sore on the sole of the foot

phrases.english: A wound on the sole of the foot.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: צינית is a sore on the sole of the foot.

steps.title: Why specifically a coin?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what is special about a סלע that makes it the remedy.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is different about a סלע?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the treatment has to be a coin and not some other object. This question opens a short back-and-forth where several answers will be tested.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If we understand why a סלע helps, we will understand what the treatment really is. The next steps try out possible reasons one at a time.

phrases.english: And what is different about a sela?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that we know what the wound is, the גמרא asks why a coin is the cure.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What quality of a סלע makes it heal the sore.

steps.title: Not just because it is hard
steps.stepSummary: If hardness were the reason, a clay shard would work. So hardness alone cannot be the answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say anything hard is good for her, then make her a clay shard!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests that the coin helps because it is hard. It immediately rejects this idea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If any hard object helped, a cheap piece of broken pottery would do the job just as well. Since the משנה mentions a coin specifically, hardness alone does not explain it.

phrases.english: If you say that any hard object
is beneficial for her,
let her make an earthenware shard!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא כֹּל מִידֵּי דַּאֲקוֹשָׁא מְעַלֵּי לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: First proposed answer to step 26, and it is rejected.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A cheaper hard object (a shard) would then work, so the coin would not be needed.

steps.title: Not just because of rust
steps.stepSummary: If the rust on a coin were the reason, a plain metal plate would work. So rust alone is not enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is because of the rust. Then make her a metal plate!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a second reason: the rust on the coin heals. It rejects this one too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A plain metal plate also rusts. If rust were the whole reason, a plate would be fine, so the coin must have something more.

phrases.english: Rather, because of the rust —
let her make a metal plate!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second proposed reason, also rejected.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A metal plate also has rust, so a coin would not be needed.

steps.title: Not just because of the image
steps.stepSummary: If the engraved image were the reason, a blank disc with an image engraved on it would work. So the image alone is not enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is because of the image. Then make her a blank coin with an image on it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a third reason: the picture stamped on the coin heals. It rejects this one as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You could take an unminted metal disc and engrave a picture on it. If the image were the whole reason, that would be enough, so the image alone does not explain why the משנה says a coin.

keyTerms.meaning: The image engraved on a coin

phrases.english: Rather, because of the image,
let her make an unminted coin!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third proposed reason, also rejected.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The image as the sole reason.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: An engraved blank disc would then work, so a minted coin would not be needed.

steps.title: אביי: all three qualities together heal
steps.stepSummary: אביי concludes that hardness, rust and image together make the coin effective.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Learn from this that all of them together are beneficial for her.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי resolves the question. No single quality is enough; the coin works because it has all three together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each other object was missing something. A shard has no rust or image. A plate has no image. A blank disc is not a real minted coin. Only a סלע combines all the qualities, which is why the משנה names it.
steps.whatToRemember: A סלע heals the foot sore because it has all three qualities together: hardness, rust and image.
steps.confusionAlert: The three rejections did not prove that hardness, rust and image are useless. They only showed that none of them works alone. אביי keeps all three.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Learn from it
that all of them together are beneficial for her.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ כּוּלְּהוּ מְעַלּוּ לָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the question of step 26 by combining the three rejected reasons.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The coin's healing comes from the combination of hardness, rust and image.

steps.title: שמואל's father's strict practices with his daughters
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about girls and threads, then tells how אבוה דשמואל did not allow his daughters to go out with threads, along with his other strict practices.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: Girls may go out with threads. שמואל's father did not let his daughters go out with threads. He did not let them sleep next to each other. He made מקוואות for them in the days of ניסן, and mats in the days of תשרי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next phrase of the משנה (girls with threads in their ears). It tells a story about how שמואל's father acted differently with his own daughters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His threads practice seems to clash with the משנה, which sets up the challenge in the next step. The other practices show how careful he was. In ניסן he made proper מקוואות, likely because the rivers were swollen with rainwater. In תשרי he put mats on the muddy riverbed so they could immerse without getting dirty.

phrases.english: The girls may go out with threads.
Shmuel's father did not allow
his daughters to go out with threads,
and did not allow them
to lie next to each other,
and he made ritual baths for them in the days of Nisan
and mats in the days of Tishrei.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַבָּנוֹת יוֹצְאוֹת בְּחוּטִין. אֲבוּהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל לָא שָׁבֵיק לְהוּ לִבְנָתֵיהּ דְּנָפְקָן בְּחוּטִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the coin case to the next clause of the משנה (step 21), girls with threads.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שמואל's father did not allow his daughters to go out with threads, and he was strict in other household matters.

steps.title: But the משנה permits threads!
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges שמואל's father: how could he forbid threads when the משנה explicitly permits them?
steps.simpleTranslation: He did not let them go out with threads? But we learned in the משנה: girls may go out with threads!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the story. The father's practice seems to go against the משנה's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says threads in girls' ears are allowed on שבת. So why would a great person like שמואל's father forbid them? The גמרא needs to explain the difference.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't we learn (in the משנה)?

phrases.english: He did not allow them to go out with threads?
But didn't we learn:
The girls may go out with threads!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the threads practice described in step 31.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה explicitly permits girls to go out with threads, so forbidding them contradicts the משנה.

steps.title: His daughters' threads were colorful
steps.stepSummary: His daughters wore colorful threads, which are a different case from the plain threads the משנה permits.
steps.simpleTranslation: The daughters of שמואל's father had colored threads.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The משנה permits plain threads, but his daughters' threads were colorful.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Colorful threads are pretty. A girl might take them out to show her friends and then carry them in the street on שבת. Plain threads give no such reason to remove them, so the משנה's permission still stands.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה permits plain threads. Colorful threads are forbidden because a girl may remove them to show them off and then carry them.
steps.whyThisMatters: This repeats a theme of the whole פרק: an ornament that a woman is likely to take off and show others is forbidden on שבת, out of concern that she will carry it.

phrases.english: The daughters of Shmuel's father
had colorful ones.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 32.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case (אוקימתא): the threads were of a different kind.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought he forbade the same plain threads the משנה permits.
steps.terutzMaskana: He forbade only colorful threads, out of concern they would be removed, shown off and carried. The משנה permits plain threads.

steps.title: He did not let his daughters sleep next to each other
steps.stepSummary: Another strict practice of אבוה דשמואל: he did not let his daughters lie down together.
steps.simpleTranslation: He did not allow them to lie next to one another.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is still listing the strict practices of אבוה דשמואל. Here it adds that he did not let his daughters sleep in the same bed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This continues the list that began in step 31, after the side discussion about colorful threads. The practice is about modesty, and the next step will ask what it was based on.

keyTerms.meaning: did not allow / did not let

phrases.english: He did not allow them
phrases.notes: "He" is אבוה דשמואל and "them" is his daughters.

phrases.english: to lie next to one another.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא שָׁבֵיק לְהוּ גָּנְיָאן גַּבֵּי הֲדָדֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the list of strict practices from step 31, after the thread discussion in steps 32-33.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אבוה דשמואל did not let his daughters sleep together.

steps.title: Does this practice support רב הונא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that this practice may support רב הונא's ruling about women who rub against one another.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say this supports רב הונא? For רב הונא said: women who rub against one another...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whether אבוה דשמואל kept his daughters apart because he held like רב הונא. It then begins quoting רב הונא's ruling. The ruling itself continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word לֵימָא introduces a proposed proof, which the גמרא often goes on to reject. The idea is that keeping the daughters apart makes the most sense if such contact carries a real halachic problem, as רב הונא holds. If he did hold like רב הונא, his practice would be evidence for that view.

keyTerms.meaning: shall we say? (opens a suggested proof, often later rejected)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume the proof works yet. לֵימָא means "shall we say?" and the גמרא may soon give another reason for the practice.

phrases.english: Shall we say this supports Rav Huna?
For Rav Huna said:
Women who rub against one another
phrases.notes: The ruling comes on the next amud: such women can't marry a כהן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what the practice in step 34 was based on and links it to רב הונא's ruling.
steps.raayaObject: רב הונא's ruling about women who rub against one another
steps.raayaSupportSource: אבוה דשמואל's practice of not letting his daughters sleep together
